subject: literature
passage: In Rajasthan, in northwestern India, the epic of the folk hero Pabuji is traditionally performed at night by a bhopa, a singer-storyteller, in front of a long painted cloth called a phad that shows scenes from the story. As the bhopa sings and plays a bowed string instrument, a companion lifts a lamp to light the part of the cloth being narrated. A complete telling can last many nights, so most performances include only part of the epic. Folklorist Kavita Sharma hypothesizes that the episodes chosen for a performance depend less on a fixed sequence passed from teacher to student than on what the hosts who invite the bhopa wish to hear.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Sharma's hypothesis?

choices.A: Bhopas who learned from the same teacher usually sing a given episode using nearly identical words.
choices.B: Phad paintings made in recent decades show more scenes from the epic than older phads do.
choices.C: Bhopas usually perform episodes in the same order, regardless of which village has invited them.
choices.D: Bhopas usually performed whichever episodes their hosts had requested, even ones from late in the story.

explanation.why: Sharma's hypothesis concerns how episodes are chosen: by hosts' wishes rather than by a fixed, inherited order. Support must show the choice following the hosts' requests, even when that breaks the story's order. Performing requested episodes from late in the story does exactly that.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This concerns the wording of an episode, not which episodes are chosen, so it does not bear on the hypothesis.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Changes in the paintings do not show how bhopas decide which episodes to perform.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Keeping the same order everywhere would suggest a fixed sequence, which weakens the hypothesis.
explanation.D: Correct. Bhopas followed their hosts' requests even when the requested episodes came late in the story, which shows hosts' wishes rather than a fixed sequence guiding the choice.
